news.title: AI tool poisoning exposes a major flaw in enterprise agent security
news.summary_raw: AI agents choose tools from shared registries by matching natural-language descriptions. But no human is verifying whether those descriptions are true. I discovered this gap when I filed Issue #141 in the CoSAI secure-ai-tooling repository. I assumed it would be treated as a single risk entry. The repository maintainer saw it differently and split my submission into two separate issues: One covering selection-time threats (tool impersonation, metadata manipulation); the other covering execution-
news.summary: An AI researcher discovered a vulnerability in the way AI agents choose tools from shared registries, where fake descriptions could be used to trick agents. This poses a risk to enterprise agent security and highlights the need for more secure AI tooling.
news.enterprise_use: This vulnerability highlights the need for IT teams to double-check the authenticity of AI tool descriptions in shared registries, to avoid being tricked into installing vulnerable agents. The most affected tool in this situation would be the registry management platform used to distribute and update AI tools.
